q: Waves are classified as progressive waves and ____.
e: Waves are either progressive, travelling out, or stationary, staying put. Waves are classified as progressive waves and stationary waves.

q: Progressive waves spread out from the ____ in which they are produced.
e: Progressive waves leave the source. Stationary waves do not spread out. Progressive waves spread out from the region in which they are produced.

q: Unlike progressive waves, stationary waves do not spread out but remain in the ____ in which they are produced.
e: A stationary wave stays in one region, so it is also called a standing wave. Unlike progressive waves, stationary waves do not spread out but remain in the region in which they are produced.

q: So stationary waves are also called ____ waves.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. So stationary waves are also called standing waves.

q: Progressive waves carry ____ through the medium.
e: A progressive wave carries energy through the medium. Energy is what this sentence is naming.

q: A stationary wave is the resultant wave by the ____ of two waves of the same type having equal amplitudes and velocities traveling in opposite directions.
e: A stationary wave needs two waves of the same type, equal amplitude and speed, travelling opposite ways. A stationary wave is the resultant wave by the superposition of two waves of the same type having equal amplitudes and velocities traveling in opposite directions.

q: When two or more waves pass the same point the resultant wave at that point is the ____ of the individual waves.
e: Superposition adds the displacements at that point. When two or more waves pass the same point the resultant wave at that point is the sum of the individual waves.
Superposition: the resultant at a point is the sum of the individual displacements. This is called principle of superposition.

q: If the resultant wave has a larger amplitude than that of individual waves, this is said to be ____ interference.
e: Interference needs coherent waves. Bright fringes are constructive; dark fringes are destructive. If the resultant wave has a larger amplitude than that of individual waves, this is said to be constructive interference.

q: If the resultant wave has a smaller amplitude than that of individual waves, this is said to be ____ interference.
e: Interference needs coherent waves. Bright fringes are constructive; dark fringes are destructive. If the resultant wave has a smaller amplitude than that of individual waves, this is said to be destructive interference.

q: One characteristic of every stationary wave pattern is that there are points along the medium, which are called ____ and antinodes.
e: Antinodes are the peaks of vibration, midway between nodes. One characteristic of every stationary wave pattern is that there are points along the medium, which are called nodes and antinodes.

q: The points that are always stationary in a stationary wave pattern are called ____.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. The points that are always stationary in a stationary wave pattern are called nodes.

q: The mid-points between successive nodes have the largest amplitudes and are called ____.
e: From one node to the next is λ/2. The same gap sits between neighbouring antinodes. The mid-points between successive nodes have the largest amplitudes and are called antinodes.

q: Nodes and antinodes always ____ and are equally spaced.
e: Antinodes are the peaks of vibration, midway between nodes. Nodes and antinodes always alternate and are equally spaced.

q: The distance between two successive nodes (or) antinodes is equal to ____.
e: Antinodes are the peaks of vibration, midway between nodes. The distance between two successive nodes (or) antinodes is equal to λ/2.

q: The distance from a node to the nearest antinode is equal to ____.
e: From a node to the next antinode is λ/4. Λ/4 is what this sentence is naming.
